lines: I rec^d^ yours of y^e^ 3^d^ Ult^o^ by the hand of M^r^ Blair, & it gave
me more comfort than I can well expreſs. We are hutted
here for y^e^ Winter, & the Men ſuffer much for want
of Shoes & Blankets. Gen^l^ Waſhington has wrote
to Congreſs in the ſtrongeſt terms, & we hope for
relief ere long. Pray tell my Mother I am in good
health, & kiſs the Children for me. I ſhall
write again by the firſt opportunity to Williamsburg.
I am, my dear Sarah, your moſt affectionate
